public_behavior: Basic and Bearer scheme names compare case-insensitively. A source treats another scheme as absent so another explicitly enabled source can recognize it. A recognized scheme requires exactly one ASCII space and one non-empty credential value; tabs, extra whitespace, and embedded whitespace are invalid. A naked recognized scheme is invalid, while a naked unknown scheme is absent.

Decode canonical padded Base64 strictly, split at the first colon, require a non-empty user-id, and preserve all remaining password bytes including later colons. The extractor does not transcode or normalize. Control octets are rejected. A caller may construct a `charset="UTF-8"` challenge, but extraction does not infer that challenge state or validate UTF-8 implicitly.

Every bearer source enforces RFC 6750 `b64token`: ASCII letters, digits, `-._~+/`, followed only by optional trailing `=`. Unicode, embedded padding, whitespace, and other bytes are invalid. `WithBearerPipe` adds only `|` and is an explicit application compatibility profile applied consistently to header and cookie sources.

Authorization is the recommended default. URI query extraction is not supported, because query credentials can be retained by logs, proxies and browser history before this package sees them. Cookie extraction is an explicit application extension. Form-body extraction is intentionally unsupported, and middleware never reads the request body. Multiple configured locations containing credentials are ambiguous rather than prioritized.

The package profile uses a non-empty key ID and a separate non-empty secret. Callers explicitly choose and name exactly one header or cookie pair. Partial pairs are invalid; duplicate values are ambiguous. The ID is routing metadata and never authenticates alone. No proprietary Authorization scheme is inferred.

Extraction succeeds only when exactly one complete credential exists across all enabled origin sources. Duplicate Authorization fields, repeated cookie values, repeated API-key components, partial pairs, and multiple populated sources fail closed. Source declaration order does not select a winner. `Proxy-Authorization` is ignored by origin credential sources.

`FormatChallenge` validates bounded token names and values, quotes every value, escapes quote and backslash, and sorts parameter names bytewise. Middleware emits each applicable challenge as its own `WWW-Authenticate` field value, preferring failure-specific challenges over configured fallbacks. If a classified credential failure has no valid challenge, middleware emits 503 instead of a non-compliant 401 and does not invent a scheme.

Absent, invalid, rejected, and ambiguous credentials map to 401 only when a valid challenge is available. Unavailable, unclassified, invalid-result, and missing-challenge failures map to a secret-safe 503. `WithOptionalAnonymous` permits anonymous access only for `ErrCredentialsAbsent`; any supplied invalid or rejected credential still fails. The package never emits 403 or `insufficient_scope` because authorization owns those decisions.

Bindings are grouped by credential kind and evaluated in declaration order. Only `ErrCredentialsRejected` falls through. Absent, invalid, ambiguous, unavailable, cancellation, and unclassified errors are terminal; unclassified errors become unavailable. A successful result must contain an authenticated principal. If all validators reject, their valid challenges are retained in declaration order.

Static Basic, bearer, and API-key authenticators derive per-instance HMAC-SHA-256 digests with random keys and compare the complete bounded candidate snapshot in constant work relative to entry count. Duplicate credentials and invalid principals reject configuration. Bearer and API-key replacement validates a complete new snapshot before atomic publication; failed replacement leaves the previous snapshot active. Basic rotation uses construction and deployment of a new immutable authenticator.

A request must not transmit a bearer token through more than one configured method. When the Authorization header and a configured bearer cookie are both populated, extraction rejects the request as ambiguous even when their values match. The RFC 6750 query method is not accepted.
Middleware generates 401 only when it can emit at least one valid applicable `WWW-Authenticate` challenge. Missing or invalid challenge metadata produces a secret-safe 503 instead of a bare 401.

`APIKeySingleHeader` reads one caller-named header, matched case-insensitively across every field spelling, and yields an `APIKeyCredential` with an empty key ID. Absence is absent, more than one value is ambiguous, and an empty, oversized, non-VCHAR or comma-bearing value is invalid. Accepted bytes are not trimmed or normalized. `WithAPIKeyRejectAuthorization` optionally makes a present API key ambiguous when any `Authorization` field is also present. The `apikey` authenticators keep requiring a key ID.

`ParseToken` hashes a non-empty pipe-free token whole with SHA-256. In the pipe form the text before the first pipe must be ASCII digits naming a positive signed 64-bit ID; leading zeros are dropped and the non-empty remainder, including later pipes, is hashed. Signs, whitespace, zero, overflow, empty parts and non-ASCII digits are malformed. `Validator` rejects a malformed token with `FailureRejected` before any lookup and otherwise returns the caller `Resolver` result unchanged. `Token.Matches` compares a raw 32-byte stored digest in constant time.
